Fig. 1. Comparison with Existing Privacy-Preserving Methods. Existing privacy-preserving methods predominantly rely on post-capture algorithms applied to original RGB videos, such as defocusing and low-resolution processing. However, these methods often fall short of fully mitigating privacy risk during data capture, as the original RGB videos still exist. In contrast, our proposed Lens Privacy Sealing (LPS) offers a physical solution that eliminates the need for generating original RGB videos, achieving privacy protection with minimal hardware modifications.

F represents the video frame set in a sample, and F̄ denotes the average frame of the sample. The indices pt, t, and st in the figure refer to the previous frame, the current frame, and the subsequent frame, respectively.

Fig. 6. Privacy-Utility Trade-off Comparison. The LPS curve (red, 0– 10 layers) forms a Pareto Frontier superior to software baselines (blue) and hardware methods (green). The x-axis is reversed: lower ACCS (better privacy) appears on the right. An ideal method maximizes ACCact while minimizing ACCS , corresponding to the top-right region. LPS achieves both strong privacy (ACCS=9.05%) and high utility (ACCact=67.90%).
